Hi Eleanor,

Thanks again for the call earlier — really appreciate you walking through FintechCo's production constraints. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned: 

Summary of what you shared:
- Primary goal: keep inference P99 latency under ~200ms for front-office UI calls (ideally target P95 < 150ms).
- Typical workload: ~500 requests/sec steady state, with daily peaks up to ~1,200 req/sec for short bursts.
- Average prompt size: ~150 tokens; responses average ~120 tokens.
- Data sensitivity: customer-facing transactions, prefer data isolation but willing to evaluate hosted if network egress/compliance controls are sufficient.

Our recommendation (high level):
- Hosted API: fastest to go live; good if you can tolerate some variability at peak unless you add burst capacity; simpler procurement.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools give predictable throughput and lower P99 latency variance — better fit if 1) you have strict latency SLOs, or 2) you need consistent peak handling without heavy throttling.

Action items / next steps:
1) Could you confirm whether the P99 200ms is a hard SLA or a target?
2) Please share any historical daily/peak qps data (I noticed you attached a small CSV during the call — if you can send a column with timestamps + qps that will help sizing).
3) I'd like to schedule a 30-45min technical session with Dev (cc'd) to walk throughput/latency tradeoffs and a quick Dedicated trial proposal. Are you available Wed or Thu next week (Aug 26-27) morning PT?

Marissa / Rishi — reviewed the CSV and put together an initial technical recommendation: 

Short answer: Dedicated capacity is the safer option to consistently meet a hard P99 < 200ms for the described workload. Hosted can hit targets most of the time but has more variance during bursts unless you commit to higher burst capacity (costly).

Sizing (initial trial footprint):
- Recommendation: 4 x A10G (or equivalent recent gen) GPUs in a dedicated pool.
- Expected throughput: ~500-700 req/sec steady per pool with < P95 120ms and P99 typically 150-220ms depending on prompt length and model choice.
- Burst handling: two additional warm slots for autoscale to absorb short 1,200 rps spikes; we can configure pre-warmed replicas to reduce cold-start jitter.

Performance notes / tradeoffs:
- Model choice matters: smaller quantized variants reduce latency significantly; we should test the customer workload against our quantized 13B family as a baseline.
- KV/prefix caching: since many of their requests share prefixes, enabling KV cache will cut effective p99 by ~20-30% for repeat patterns.
- Network hop: Dedicated within their region reduces network variance vs cross-region hosted calls.

SLA & cost ballpark:
- SLA: we can offer a P99 SLA for Dedicated with an uptime/latency credit program (details handled by sales/legal).
- Ballpark cost: Dedicated trial (4x A10G reserved for a month) ~ $20k- $28k/mo depending on GPU family and support tier. Hosted with conservative burst capacity to match peaks likely runs similar costs but with higher per-token charges and potential throttling during simultaneous customer peaks.

Next technical steps:
1) Run a short perf POC (2 weeks) using their sample traffic to measure real P95/P99 on our quantized model variants.
2) If results look good, convert trial into a 3-month pilot with an SLA.

—
